entry.title: build(filecheck): replace imagemin with sharp
entry.content:
Description

Update filecheck to compress JPEG, PNG, and GIF images with sharp and optimize SVGs with SVGO directly. Remove imagemin dependencies and temporary compression files.

Motivation

Simplify image compression dependencies and remove standalone binary installation scripts.

Additional details

Regression tests cover format preservation, GIF frames and timing, transparency, EXIF orientation, and file size limits.

Behavior changes compared to imagemin:

  • JPEG: mozjpeg's cjpeg reused the quality of JPEG input and kept its metadata, so it never flagged a JPEG in this repo. sharp re-encodes at quality 75 with mozjpeg optimizations and applies the EXIF orientation before stripping metadata. A full run over files/ newly flags 15 existing files (13 JPEGs, 1 PNG, 1 GIF), which CI only reports once a PR touches them.
  • GIF: gifsicle was lossless. sharp re-quantizes frames: 55 of the 58 GIFs in this repo re-encode pixel-identical, the other 3 show small colour shifts or merge a near-duplicate frame while keeping its delay, and none of them exceeds the compression threshold.

Related issues and pull requests

entry.title: Fix typos in CSS docs: unbalanced parentheses, its/it's, affect/effect
entry.content:
Description

Fixes 25 small typos across 24 CSS pages. Each change is a one- or two-character fix; no wording is rewritten.

Commits are split by kind of fix:

  1. Unbalanced or misplaced parentheses (13): a missing ( or ), an extra one, a doubled ((, or a ) that ended up inside inline code
  2. its/it's and affect/effect mix-ups (9)
  3. Stray articles and punctuation (3)
All changes
Page Kind Reason
Guides/Colors/Applying_color paren '(such as the addition of ...' never closes
Guides/Colors/Color_values paren outer paren never closes

Reference/Properties/cx paren doubled opening paren
Reference/Properties/cy paren doubled opening paren
Reference/Properties/flex-grow paren paren leaked into inline code
Reference/Properties/overlay paren extra closing paren
Reference/Properties/r paren doubled opening paren
Reference/Values/absolute-size paren extra closing paren
Reference/Values/image/image paren '(and prevented the image from repeating ...' never closes
Guides/Gaps/Defining_gaps affect verb affect
Guides/Gaps/Defining_gaps article stray 'a'
Guides/Masking/Multiple_masks affect verb affect
Guides/Values_and_units/Numeric_data_types its possessive
Reference/Properties/appearance affect verb affect
Reference/Properties/flex-line-count affect verb affect
Reference/Properties/mask-clip affect noun effect
Reference/Properties/timeline-trigger-source article a → an
Reference/Properties/will-change its possessive
Reference/Values/basic-shape/shape affect noun effect
Reference/Values/calc-keyword its contraction
Reference/Values/easing-function/steps punct comma spacing (alt text)

Motivation

These typos make sentences harder to read. For the parentheses, I checked each sentence to decide whether a paren was missing or extra, and looked at the git history where the intent wasn't obvious.

Additional details

I found these by scanning for unbalanced parentheses and a few common grammar patterns, then reviewed every hit by hand. I'm planning to send similar fixes for other areas in separate PRs, one per area, so each one goes to a single team.

entry.title: Update size="1" note for multiple select
entry.content:
Description

Updates the size="1" paragraph in the "Accessibility concerns" section of the multiple attribute page. It no longer tells authors never to use size="1" on a multiple select, since that's now the opt-in for a drop-down multi-select. It still mentions the old behavior in browsers that haven't shipped this yet, and keeps the advice to tell users that more than one option can be selected.

Motivation

The page currently says "Don't do that" about <select multiple size="1">, which contradicts the newer HTML behavior where this markup gives a drop-down multi-select.

Additional details

  • HTML spec change: whatwg/html#11460
  • Chrome Status: https://chromestatus.com/feature/5412736871825408
  • Firefox: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1988022, WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=309606 (and WebKit/WebKit#75555 for macOS)

I kept the sentence about browsers without support because of the interop question in the issue. Happy to drop it and just remove the paragraph if you'd prefer.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #45988

entry.title: IDBDatabase: make the upgrade example work for existing databases
entry.content:
Description

Reworks the onupgradeneeded handler in the IDBDatabase example so it handles upgrades from an older version, not just first-time creation:

  • The handler now checks event.oldVersion and applies each upgrade step the user hasn't had yet. Version 1 creates the toDoList store and its date/time indexes; version 2 adds the notified index to the existing store, which it gets from the upgrade transaction (DBOpenRequest.transaction.objectStore()) instead of calling createObjectStore() again.
  • The open() call asks for version 2 to match.
  • Fixes a node.appendChild typo (the variable is note), plus a missing full stop in a comment.

Motivation

As the issue says, the old handler always called createObjectStore("toDoList"), so it only worked when the database didn't exist yet. Bumping the version for anyone with an existing database threw a ConstraintError and aborted the upgrade. I checked this with fake-indexeddb: after creating the database at version 1, the old handler fails on the upgrade to version 2 with ConstraintError, while the new handler produces the same six indexes both for a fresh install at version 2 and for an upgrade from version 1.

Additional details

IndexedDB spec, IDBVersionChangeEvent.oldVersion (0 for a new database) and IDBOpenDBRequest.transaction during an upgrade.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #26638

entry.title: New guide: Fetch priority
entry.content:
Description

Adds a guide on fetch priority under Web/Performance/Guides, with a sidebar entry and a line on the Performance landing page.

Motivation

#14803 asks for a topic on prioritizing resource requests. There's reference for fetchpriority, the priority option of fetch(), preload and the Priority header, but no page that ties them together. The guide covers how browsers pick a default priority, how resources get discovered, and where each tool fits.

Two things in the issue came out different when I checked them. There's no fetchpriority on <iframe> in the HTML spec or in BCD, and Request has no priority property, only the init option. The page says both.

Additional details

Chrome's defaults come from the table in https://web.dev/articles/fetch-priority and Firefox's from https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/networking/http/prioritization.html. Browser-specific behavior is attributed to the browser, and version numbers are left to the reference pages.

I ran the examples in Chrome 154 against a local server and read each request's priority over the DevTools protocol. They matched what the page says, with one exception: I couldn't get headless Chrome to raise hidden carousel slides to High, so that sentence leans on the web.dev article. Nothing was tested in Firefox or Safari.

The rel="preload" reference page says a preload is "downloaded and cached with a higher priority", which doesn't hold for images in Chrome. I left that page alone here and can send a small follow-up.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #14803
